Subject: Re: Request: extra sandbox credits for QuickFabric dev team — initial fraud triage

Thanks for the ping. Short summary of findings after pulling the signups and matching session logs:

Findings (sample size: 34 signups)
- 18 accounts use disposable/forwarding domains (examples: onboard-345@mailinator.com, testusr+cf1@disposablemail.org).
- 12 accounts show the same device fingerprint (same screen/resolution/os+browser hash) across multiple emails — suggests browser automation or shared VM images.
- 9 accounts initiated signups from the same /24 IP block over a 3-hour window; reverse DNS indicates cloud-labs provider (likely CI/CD runner pool).
- Behavioral signals: identical user-agent strings and near-instant first request to /v1/chat/completions immediately after signup for 15 accounts — consistent with scripted testing.
- No confirmed payment or corporate-domain verification for the majority; only 4 accounts used quickfabric.com addresses.

Recommendation:
- Deny bulk 25-token full grant as-is (high risk of abuse).
- Offer a provisional, rate-limited sandbox pack: 5 developer tokens for 10 days, per-seat rate limit of 60 RPM, and require domain verification for any expansion.
- Ask QuickFabric to provide a CSV of the 34 accounts (we can review and whitelist any legitimate corporate addresses).
- If QuickFabric can provide a PO or SSO assertion for partner cohort, escalate to sales for a standard reserved grant.

Attached: signup_csv_sample.csv (sanitized sample), session_logs_20270409.txt (obfuscated IPs).

Let me know if you want a stricter posture (zero issuance) — this recommendation balances support for their testing needs with fraud protection.

— Dev Patel
Fraud & Abuse Ops | Redwood Inference

Hi Liam — thanks for the patience and for offering the account list. We dug into the signups and observed a mix of legitimate and high-risk signals (summary below).

Summary:
- Several accounts appear to be legitimate QuickFabric employees (4 confirmed @quickfabric.com).
- Majority of the 34 accounts show disposable domains, shared device fingerprints, or signup bursts from a cloud /24 block that usually corresponds to automated test runners.

What we can do now:
1) Provisional grant: 5 developer tokens for 10 days, rate-limited (60 RPM per seat). This is immediately available and intended to support smoke/load tests without exposing a large token pool to potential abuse.
2) Fast-track expansion: If you share the CSV of the 34 accounts and identify verified corporate emails (or provide an SSO assertion / PO), we will whitelist qualified accounts and convert to a larger short-term grant.

Please upload the CSV to the Drive link below (or attach in reply) and I'll get our ops team to review within 6 hours of receipt: https://drive.redwood.com/secure/quickfabric-logs-20270409

If you prefer a zero-issuance posture, say the word and we'll hold. We want to help your partner onboarding but need to manage platform risk.

Thanks — I can also set up a quick 15-min call to walk through the verification steps.

— Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
